correctness.rationale: The four-row, six-column incidence matrix for three strict alternatives is totally unimodular by a full 15-row-subset Ghouila-Houri signing certificate, also checked via all 209 possible nonempty square minors in ranking_quota_verifier.py. A nonempty bounded integer-RHS system with source-multiplicity upper bounds has an integral point, proving every floor/ceiling pairwise quota simultaneously for any n and 1<=k<=n without repetition. For m=4,n=4,k=2 the explicit four-ballot witness violates exactly one balanced pairwise quota for each of the six voter pairs. Exhaustive finite computations enumerate all 17550 anonymous ranking multisets directly and independently test the tied-comparison characterization on all 10626 distinct-rank sets; both return 690 obstructions, with 30 alternative-relabeling orbits. The included verifier actually executed successfully. The arbitrary-n assertion rests on the proof, not finite tests.

value.rationale: An actual-voter subset preserving all pairwise preference shares is a natural and stronger representation demand than generated rankings, with applications to deliberative sampling and representative benchmark metrics. Exact balanced subsampling is possible for every sample size and arbitrary input for three alternatives because of a special total-unimodular rank-incidence structure, but fails already at the next candidate count. The first n=4,k=2 obstruction layer has a fully reproducible exact census (690/17550, 30 symmetry classes), quantifying the frequency and diversity of failure. This is a motivated sharp structural boundary and complete first-layer invariant, not a routine numeric gain or restatement of a prior theorem.
